clinic.name: Parkway Orthodontics
clinic.review_summary: Patients love the evening and Saturday appointments, the warm front desk and how clearly the doctor explains treatment. A few say it costs more than nearby offices.

price_sheet.personality: Friendly and chatty, but always checks with a manager before matching a price or giving a discount.
facts: Two of the assistants speak Spanish, and forms come in Spanish too.
The office offers Invisalign clear aligners as well as braces, for about the same price.
For a patient under 18, a parent or guardian signs the plan and can make the payments.

clinic.name: Sunrise Orthodontic Studio
clinic.review_summary: Known for low, upfront prices, early morning visits and quick appointments. Some reviewers mention the office feels rushed and there are no after-work appointments.

price_sheet.personality: Brisk and busy, gives short answers, and wants to wrap up the call quickly.
facts: There is no sedation, but the doctor uses numbing gel and gives wax and a comfort kit for sore days.
The office only does metal and ceramic braces, no clear aligners.
A parent or guardian can set up and pay the plan for a patient under 18.

clinic.name: Lakeside Family Orthodontics
clinic.review_summary: Families like the Saturday hours and the patient staff. Several reviews say the office is firm on pricing and rarely offers deals.

price_sheet.personality: Polite and patient, but says no to most discounts and sticks to the listed price.
facts: The office offers Invisalign clear aligners, usually a few hundred dollars more than braces.
Many patients are teens, and parents can pay with the monthly plan.
For nervous patients the team does a slow first visit and can use numbing gel; there is no sedation.
